assertionOwnership.wrapperRows: 16 wrapped-event methods each retain two independent runtime cases: complete nondefault arguments plus output checks, and required arguments plus explicit defaults and no final output.
assertionOwnership.resultIdentity: 4 aggregate-returning methods each retain two independent runtime cases. The complete failure/block payload and absent-output aggregate must be returned by identity.
assertionOwnership.specializedSemantics: 7 output semantic cases retain deny/context, systemMessage/defaults, permission decision/error handling, PermissionDenied literal fields and SubagentStop allow behavior, and independently add expansion ampersand escaping, batch stop behavior and stop-reason formatting.
assertionOwnership.unchanged: Construction, initialization/reload, event handler/registry accessors, enable/disable, registered hooks, event queries including session hooks, and messages provider cases are unchanged.
assertionOwnership.positiveLabels: Distinct arbitrary prompts, tool names, notification values and context strings that reached the same branch are represented by the explicit required/full argument rows. This is a behavioral partition change rather than a claim that all old concrete inputs remain. PostToolUseFailure also consolidates the former explicit isInterrupt=false row into true and omitted/undefined rows; the wrapper has no branch on this value.

limits: A failed earlier assertion can mask later assertions within its event-specific contract; each method and missing-output partition remains separately named.

Some positive-value labels and aggregate allow payloads are consolidated into representative full/default forwarding and failure-result identity checks; mutation and semantic review are required before retention.
StopFailure and PostCompact wrappers lacked cases in this baseline file and remain outside this bounded redesign.
